text:
Alex Ramos: Quick RFC follow-up — proposal for a pluggable kernel API that cleanly supports both grouped-query (GQA) and multi-query (MQA) paths. Wanted to capture tradeoffs + a rollout plan. :thinking:

Marta Li: SG. Can you sketch the minimal boundary you have in mind?

Alex Ramos: Minimal idea: a Kernel trait with 3 responsibilities: capability check, prepare (batching/KV layout), and steady-state run. Sketch: ```interface Kernel { supports(model_meta): bool; prepare(inputs, batch_ctx): PreparedKernel; run(prepared, kv_cache, opts): OutputStream; }```

Cheng Wu: That looks fine high-level. Key question: who owns the KV cache layout translation when switching kernels mid-request?

Alex Ramos: Good point — my leaning: runtime manages a canonical KV layout; kernel implements adapters for its preferred memory ordering. That keeps routing simple but forces kernels to implement conversion fast-paths.

Samir Patel: Conversion can be costly if we memcpy large KV slices. We should opt for on-the-fly zero-copy views when possible and only do copy-on-write for incompatible quant/layout.

Marta Li: Agree. Also need to define what 'supports' checks. Model config + quantization + seq-length profile? We can't call into kernels for every request.

Alex Ramos: Proposed supports signature: supports(model_family, quant_profile, max_seq_hint, featureset_flags) -> {ok, reason_code}. Runtime caches supports() by model-version + quant_profile + instance-type.

Dana O'Neill: From ops side: exposing a simple metric when a kernel returns "reason_code=FALLBACK_MEM_LAYOUT" would be super helpful in alerts. Otherwise tracers will be noisy.

Cheng Wu: On testing: we need a compatibility matrix job that runs small synthesized sequences across all kernel permutations (GQA vs MQA, fp16 vs int8, small/large seq). Otherwise subtle correctness bugs slip in.

Alex Ramos: Yep — plan: unit kernel harness + e2e runner that replays a fixed corpus. If mismatch detected, harness dumps KV diffs + per-token hashes. Also include perf microbenchmarks (latency + tail percentile).

Samir Patel: Rollout plan idea: feature-flagged kernel toggles per model-version. Start with canary 1% traffic, perf guard rails (p50/p95 within threshold), and automatic rollback if error rate > X or perf regressed. Also an operator command to force-fallback for a model/version.

Marta Li: One more API thought — allow kernel to advertise batching preferences: prefers_continuous_batching: true/false, ideal_batch_size, prefetch_kv_window. Scheduler can use that to avoid pathological batching mixing GQA and MQA patterns.

Alex Ramos: Perfect — that gives scheduler signals without hard-coding.

Dana O'Neill: Ops request: make sure kernel load/unload is observable in the console (version, model compatibility, memory use). We'll need limits per-host to avoid OOMs when enabling many kernels.

Cheng Wu: Implementation worries: number of kernel permutations explodes (model variants x quant x gqa/mqa). We should prioritize: 1) most used model families, 2) int8/normal quant, 3) GQA for high-throughput customers. Others on-demand.

Alex Ramos: Action items: 1) I'll update the RFC with the Kernel interface + supports signature and the canary rollout steps. 2) @Marta to spec the compatibility test matrix (small initial set). 3) @Cheng to prototype KV adapter primitives (zero-copy view + COW path). 4) @Dana to outline ops dashboard rows + alerts.

Marta Li: I can do the matrix, will add a minimal required corpus and target pass/fail criteria.

Cheng Wu: I'll spike on KV adapters this week. Will push a small prototype in eng-runtime branch and link here.

Dana O'Neill: I'll draft dashboard rows and an alert playbook.

infra-bot: Deploy check: nightly CI job scheduled for kernel-compat-matrix at 03:00 UTC.

Alex Ramos: Cool, thanks everyone. I'll post the updated RFC link once done. :thumbsup:
